Q: Flags or arguments to configure Clangd in Visual Studio Code A:

The behaviour of inserting placeholders for function (and template) arguments can be disabled by passing --function-arg-placeholders=0 to clangd. In VSCode, you would do this in VSCode's settings under "clangd.arguments".

Regarding completion of keywords like template and typename, this does work for me out of the box, though note that the completion items have the "snippet" kind, e.g. for template, the item label is "template declaration" but when you choose it only template is inserted followed by a space, putting the cursor in the right position for you to type the rest of the declaration.

If completion is not working as intended in some specific scenario, I would suggest filing an issue at https://github.com/clangd/clangd/issues/ with details.

Q: Query tuning: counting distinct matching rows across tables A:

With no indexes, the execution plan will require some form of sorting to supporting both the DISTINCT and JOIN (likely merge-join) operations.

I tried the following approach that could possibly be executed using a single sort:

SELECT county, COUNT(*)
FROM (
    SELECT county, PAON, street, city
    FROM (
        SELECT county, PAON, street, city, p24 = 1, p25 = 0
        FROM ShortPricePaidData2024
        UNION ALL
        SELECT county, PAON, street, city, p24 = 0, p25 = 1
        FROM ShortPricePaidData2025
    ) U
    GROUP BY county, PAON, street, city
    HAVING MAX(p24) = 1
    AND MAX(p25) = 1
) G
GROUP BY county
ORDER BY county

My intent was to trigger a single sort after the UNION ALL. However, the actual execution plan still included two separate source data sorts, and the execution time was marginally worse than your original posted query.

I believe your original query may be as good as it gets without indexes. If this is a frequently recurring query, you should really consider adding supporting indexes.

See this db<>fiddle. Search the execution plan XML for QueryTimeStats to see CpuTime statistics.

Q: How to get Clangd working properly with Visual Studio Code on Windows A:

I got clangd to work on Visual Studio Code with the Mingw-w64 compiler, CMake, and SFML by doing the following:

  1. Install the clangd extension in Visual Studio Code.

  2. CMake must create the compile_commands.json file. This is done via set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON), which you already described.

  3. Create a .clangd file in the root folder of your project.

  4. Add the following to the .clangd file:

    CompileFlags:
  Add: [
    --target=x86_64-w64-mingw32,
  ]

  5. At this point, you might have to restart Visual Studio Code. It should now recognize SFML, as well as the MinGW standard library header files.

Q: pg_relation_size tells me column doesn't exist A:

Before running the query, one need to connect to the database

Step1: Connect to the server

Step2: Connect to the database

<username>=>\c databasename

Step3: Run the query
